title: Seedream 5.5 on Flick: Edits, Transparency and Price | Flick
summary: Seedream 5.5 is ByteDance's new image model for repeated edits and transparent PNGs. What it costs on Flick, how to use it, and what our tests showed.
body_markdown:
Seedream 5.5 is ByteDance's new image model, released on November 9, 2026. Its pitch is editing: change one thing in a picture, again and again, and the rest stays put. It also makes images with a real transparent background. On Flick it runs in[Generate Image](https://flick.art/docs/generate-image) and[Edit Image](https://flick.art/docs/editimage) , costs 6 credits a new image, and is included on the Free plan.


This guide covers what Seedream 5.5 costs on Flick, how to use it, and what happened when we edited one film still six times in a row, made two transparent assets, and reran the six prompts from our[Seedream 5.0 Pro guide](https://flick.art/blog/seedream-5-pro-guide) .


## Quick answer: when should you use Seedream 5.5?


Use Seedream 5.5 when you want to build a shot up change by change, or need a cut-out prop or title. Then:


1. **Add an image node and choose Seedream 5.5.** Tick Transparent Background if you need a cut-out asset.
2. **Quote every word you want shown, and add "no extra text".** It spells quoted words well but adds words of its own.
3. **Edit one change per round.** End each edit with "Keep everything else exactly the same", at 9 credits an edit at 1.5K.

## What is Seedream 5.5?


ByteDance Seed describes three upgrades ([ByteDance Seed](https://seed.bytedance.com/en/blog/more-realistic-images-more-stable-editing-across-100-rounds-introducing-seedream-5-5) ):


- **Stable multi-round editing.** Unedited regions are kept "at the pixel level", with no colour shift, across 100 rounds of edits in its demo.
- **Native RGBA output.** Images come with an alpha channel, full and partial transparency, so a generated element can go straight into a layout without background removal.
- **More realistic images and clearer text.** More natural light, skin and materials, and better dense small text. ByteDance reports a severe text corruption rate of 0.4% and a minor one of 1.7% in its own Chinese and English tests.


ByteDance also says Seedream 5.5 beat Seedream 5.0 Pro on quality and usability in all six use cases it tested, and that a Pro version of Seedream 5.5 will follow. Those are its evaluations, not ours. Seedream 5.5 reached Flick on November 12, 2026.


## How to use Seedream 5.5 on Flick


1. **Add an image node.**[Generate an image](https://flick.art/docs/generate-image) walks through it.
2. **Choose Seedream 5.5** in the model picker.
3. **Set resolution and ratio.** 1.5K is the default (2048 × 1152 at 16:9 in our tests); 2K costs 1.5 times as much.
4. **Tick Transparent Background** if you want a cut-out PNG instead of a full frame.
5. **Connect references if you need them.** Up to 10. In[Edit Image](https://flick.art/docs/editimage) , call them Figure 1, Figure 2 and so on in the prompt.
6. **Write the prompt.** Put every word you want shown in quotes, and say "no extra text" if the picture should carry only those words.


Seedream 5.5 also accepts[Flickpedia styles](https://flick.art/docs/visual-styles) . We have not tested a style on it yet, so the tests below use plain prompts.


## Test 1: the six prompts from our Seedream 5.0 Pro guide


We reran the six prompts from the[Seedream 5.0 Pro guide](https://flick.art/blog/seedream-5-pro-guide) word for word, at 1.5K, with no reference or style. Every quoted word came back spelled right, including the accent in "Café" and the Japanese sign. But in four of six images Seedream 5.5 also added readable text nobody asked for.


An old lighthouse keeper with a grey beard sits by a rainy window at night, his face lit by an oil lamp at the left edge


**A film still lit by one lamp.** It framed him head and shoulders, the close-up the prompt asked for, with one oil lamp and rain on the glass. The "grey stubble" grew into a full beard. No text.


A vintage poster with a pale title over a green aurora and a lit lighthouse on a cliff at sunset, studio logos and a credits block at the bottom


**A poster with a title and tagline.** "THE LAST LIGHTHOUSE" and "Every light goes out eventually." came back exact. It also added "A SCI-FI MOVIE", two side taglines, two studio logos and an eight-line credits block. The top five credit lines read cleanly; the bottom three are unreadable.


A lit café sign reading 夜明けの喫茶店 and Dawn Café over a dark shopfront on an empty rainy Tokyo lane, a chalkboard by the door


**Japanese and English on one sign.** It wrote "夜明けの喫茶店" and "Dawn Café" with the accent, which Seedream 5.0 Pro dropped. The chalkboard reads "Coffee" and "500円" with a few lines of scribbled small print between them.


A six-panel comic of a girl in a pink hoodie and a silver robot dog wading through a flooded city, ending with her reaching for a kite


**A six-panel comic page.** "It flew this way!", "Woof?" and "Found it!" landed in panels 1, 3 and 6, spelled right. But "It flew this way!" was repeated in panels 2, 4 and 5, it painted three signs of its own (one reads "SIGN STRONGER OVER HERE..."), and the gutters came out white, not the black we asked for.


A fox in glasses and a plaid scarf reads a map by a lantern and a campfire in a snowy watercolour forest, a four-line caption on white paper above


**A watercolour picture book page.** It left far more white paper than Seedream 5.0 Pro: 43% of the picture is near-white, against 22% for 5.0 Pro, measured the same way on both files. It also wrote a four-line story caption and labelled a crate "Supplies", a tin "Hot Cocoa" and two trail signs.


A pencil storyboard of four panels: a harbor at dawn, a fisherman with a net, a fish held up to the light, a man facing a town, each with a typed label


**A storyboard sheet with labels.** Every word of the four labels came back right, with each hyphen drawn as a longer spaced dash. The "glowing fish" has a sparkle on it rather than a glow.


## Test 2: six edits in a row


This is what Seedream 5.5 is built for. We took the lighthouse keeper above and edited him six times, each round fed the previous result, one change at a time: a wool cap, the lamp swapped for a candle, a cream sweater, wire glasses, a turn to camera, a red scarf. Every prompt ended with "Keep everything else exactly the same."


Six frames of the lighthouse keeper, each one edit further: a dark wool cap, the oil lamp replaced by a candle, a cream cable-knit sweater, round wire glasses, a turn to face the camera, a red scarf


- **Every edit landed,** in the round it was asked for, and he is the same man from the first frame to the last.
- **The rest held still.** We measured two patches of the window that no prompt touched: they moved 0.6 to 0.8 levels out of 255 per round, about 3 after six rounds, close to the noise of saving a JPEG again.
- **For comparison,** Seedream 5.0 Pro on the same six edits moved those patches 1.0 to 7.0 levels per round and up to 14.9 in total, and added the candle's reflection to the window. The side by side is in our[Seedream 5.5 vs Seedream 5.0 Pro](https://flick.art/blog/seedream-5-5-vs-seedream-5-pro) test.


The six edits cost 54 credits at 1.5K, 9 each. For a film, this means you can dress a character and a set change by change without regenerating the face you already like.


## Test 3: transparent backgrounds


We ticked Transparent Background and asked for two assets: a brass ship's lantern and the title "THE LAST LIGHTHOUSE" with a soft green glow. Both came back as PNGs with a real alpha channel.


Left: a brass ship's lantern with a lit flame, cut out and placed on a coral background. Right: the words THE LAST LIGHTHOUSE in pale green letters on a dark green cloud, placed on a blue background


- **The lantern cut out cleanly.** 74% of its pixels are fully transparent, the rope handle has a clean edge, and the soft shadow under its base is kept as a partly see-through layer.
- **The frosted glass stayed solid.** The glass panes are fully opaque, so a background never shows through them, even though ByteDance says partial transparency is supported.
- **The glow became a plate.** "Soft green glow" came back as an opaque dark cloud behind the letters. Ask for the words alone, then add the glow in your edit.


Each asset cost 6 credits.


## What people use Seedream 5.5 for on Flick


Mostly editing. Of the 1,017 Seedream 5.5 images Flick users made from November 12 to 21, 2026, 908 (89%) were edits of an existing picture rather than new images from a prompt.


Two more things from the same period, counted across all accounts:


- **Edits are blocked more often.** About one in five edit requests (217 of 1,127) ended in a content moderation block, against 4 of 113 plain prompt requests. See[Why a generation was flagged](https://flick.art/docs/why-flagged) for what to change.
- **How long it takes.** Half the finished edits came back within 29 seconds and nine in ten within 90 seconds. That includes Flick's queue, so treat it as what to expect, not the model's speed.


## Prompting Seedream 5.5


- **Say "no extra text".** It added taglines, logos, signs and a caption across four of our six tests.
- **Quote every word you need.** Every quoted line came back spelled right, accents and Japanese included.
- **Check the fine print.** The poster's large lines were clean; its smallest credit lines were not.
- **One change per edit.** Ask for a single change and end with "Keep everything else exactly the same".
- **Keep cut-outs plain.** Describe just the object for a transparent asset; glows and glass came back opaque.
- **Call references Figure 1, Figure 2.** That is how Seedream 5.5 reads several references in Edit Image.


## Seedream 5.5 vs other image models on Flick


### Seedream 5.5


Pros:


- Holds a picture still across repeated edits: under one level in 255 per round in our test.
- Real transparent PNGs from one setting.
- Spelled every quoted word right, including an accent Seedream 5.0 Pro dropped.
- 6 credits a new image, less than half of Seedream 5.0 Pro.


Cons:


- Adds readable text you did not ask for, in four of our six tests.
- Fine print can turn unreadable.
- Glows and frosted glass came back opaque on transparent assets.
- 2K is the top resolution.


### When to pick something else


- **A poster or page with only your words:** Seedream 5.0 Pro added much less unrequested text in the same tests. See our[Seedream 5.0 Pro guide](https://flick.art/blog/seedream-5-pro-guide) .
- **4K output:** GPT Image 2.6 or Nano Banana 2.1. See our[Nano Banana 2.1 guide](https://flick.art/blog/nano-banana-2-1-guide) .
- **Staging a shot inside a location image with many references:** Krea 3. See our[Krea 3 guide](https://flick.art/blog/krea-3-guide) .


## Common mistakes


- **Expecting only the words you quoted.** Add "no extra text".
- **Asking for several changes in one edit.** Chain single edits instead.
- **Asking for a glow on a cut-out.** It comes back as a solid plate.
- **Connecting a reference you do not need.** Any reference bills the edit price, 9 credits instead of 6.
- **Rendering at 2K while still exploring.** 1.5K is 6 credits, 2K is 9.

## Frequently Asked Questions


What is Seedream 5.5?


ByteDance Seed's image generation and editing model, released on November 9, 2026. It keeps unedited parts of a picture stable across many edits and outputs transparent PNGs.


How much does Seedream 5.5 cost on Flick?


6 credits a new image at 1.5K and 9 at 2K. An edit, or any run with a reference connected, costs 9 at 1.5K and 14 at 2K.


Is Seedream 5.5 free on Flick?


It is included on the Free plan. Each image uses credits; a new account gets 100 credits, and free accounts get 100 more each day.


Can Seedream 5.5 make transparent backgrounds?


Yes. Tick Transparent Background and it returns a PNG with an alpha channel. Glows and frosted glass came back opaque in our tests.


How many times can you edit an image with Seedream 5.5?


ByteDance demonstrates 100 edits in a row. We ran six on Flick, and the parts we never asked to change moved less than one level in 255 per round.


Can Seedream 5.5 write text in images?


Yes. It spelled a poster title, comic balloons, storyboard labels and a Japanese and English sign correctly. It also adds text of its own, so ask for no extra text.


Why was my Seedream 5.5 edit blocked?


Edit requests are blocked far more often than plain prompts: about one in five on Flick from November 12 to 21, 2026. See Why a generation was flagged.


What is the difference between Seedream 5.5 and Seedream 5.0 Pro?


Seedream 5.5 costs 6 credits against 14, adds transparent output, and edited more steadily in our test. Seedream 5.0 Pro added less unrequested text.
